# Tracing a symptom to a limiting stage

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `observability-request-diagnosis` · **Observability, Performance & Reliability** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S01-Q046](#S01-Q046)

<p>Under many concurrent requests, how would you identify the actual bottleneck in a .NET application? Explain the evidence that distinguishes your leading hypotheses.</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Use correlated telemetry to distinguish the cause of production latency or resource pressure.</p>

<ul>
<li>Connect logs, metrics and traces across a cross-stack request.</li>
<li>Form competing hypotheses for latency, memory growth or worker pressure.</li>
<li>Interpret tail measurements and select a discriminating check.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Request pipeline, middleware and filters](aspnet-request-pipeline.md)

<p>Begin with the request that is slow, then connect its stages with aggregate resource evidence. Correlation makes a path inspectable, while distributions and targeted runtime checks tell you which suspected cause fits more than one anecdotal trace.</p>

<a id="S05-Q028"></a>

### S05-Q028 · Foundation

<p>How do logs, metrics and traces answer different questions when diagnosing an application?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q028](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q028)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q028](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q028)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Distinguish logs, metrics and traces.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Use one request or incident to compare the information each type provides. Explain the evidence you need, not just three definitions.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose an evidence type from a specific diagnostic question.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a distributed ASP.NET Core application as context; collection products and configuration are not prescribed.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects each evidence type to an observable symptom or causal question.</li>
<li>Explains one blind spot and how another evidence type helps test the hypothesis.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating a large volume of logs as sufficient visibility into every request and system trend.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you collect first if a latency metric worsens but existing logs show no error?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q030"></a>

### S05-Q030 · Mechanism

<p>How do correlation IDs and distributed trace context help connect observations across a request?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q030](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q030)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q030](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q030)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain correlation IDs and distributed trace context.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Define what each identifier refers to and how it crosses a boundary. A trace context is information used to connect parts of distributed execution.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain observation identity and propagation without confusing it with business identity.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the propagation format and instrumentation stack; distinguish a request, a trace, an operation and a business message when applicable. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Uses a concrete multi-hop example to explain identifier scope and propagation.</li>
<li>Describes a check for missing or incorrectly reused context across independent operations.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming any shared string automatically supplies a correct distributed trace.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you handle context when one operation creates several independent downstream tasks?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q034"></a>

### S05-Q034 · Mechanism

<p>Why can p95 and p99 latency reveal a production problem that an average hides, and when can those percentiles mislead you?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q034](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q034)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q034](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q034)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Why are p95/p99 latency measurements more useful than averages for many production investigations?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A percentile describes a position in a distribution. Explain it with a small set of request times and connect the interpretation to affected users.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Interpret latency distributions and state the limits of the measurement.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Establish the request population, time window, sample size and aggregation method; do not assume every workload needs the same metric.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains average and tail measurements using the same concrete dataset.</li>
<li>Checks how sampling or aggregation could change the apparent conclusion.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating a percentile as the latency of every request or as automatically meaningful for a tiny sample.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you verify before comparing p99 values from two differently sampled services?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q032"></a>

### S05-Q032 · Application

<p>Which telemetry would you collect to understand latency, errors, dependency behavior and resource pressure?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q032](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q032)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q032](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q032)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What telemetry would you collect for latency, errors, dependencies and resource pressure?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Connect each observation to a decision or hypothesis. Resource pressure means demand approaching a resource’s practical capacity, not one unexplained high-utilization number.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design a telemetry set that supports diagnosis rather than collecting data without a purpose.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a service with a database and external dependency; clarify sampling, labels, retention and privacy constraints.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Maps each signal to a distinct failure or performance question.</li>
<li>Explains how to test visibility while controlling collection overhead and unnecessary data.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Listing metric names without stating which symptom or decision each supports.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you verify that telemetry remains useful during a dependency outage?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q029"></a>

### S05-Q029 · Application

<p>How would you trace one request across the frontend, gateway, multiple backend services and database calls?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q029](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q029)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q029](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q029)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How would you trace one request across frontend, gateway, multiple backend services and database calls?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Show how observations at each hop can be connected to the same request and how you would localize missing time or missing evidence.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design an end-to-end observation path across service ownership boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Include every named hop; clarify synchronous and asynchronous boundaries and telemetry access without assuming an existing tracing setup.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces evidence propagation across the complete request path.</li>
<li>Tests a deliberately broken propagation boundary and explains what remains observable.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Drawing a request path while omitting how observations from different services are connected.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you investigate a database call that appears in logs but is missing from the request trace?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q031"></a>

### S05-Q031 · Failure cases

<p>How would you investigate a slow API before choosing an optimization?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q031](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q031)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q031](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q031)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How would you investigate a slow API?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Begin with a measurable symptom, then explain which observations distinguish competing causes. Keep diagnosis separate from proposing a familiar fix.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Build a falsifiable investigation and verify the effect of a change.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify endpoint, affected traffic, time window and what “slow” means; separate client-observed time from backend measurements.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Prioritizes hypotheses and selects evidence that can rule them out.</li>
<li>Compares a proposed change against a representative baseline and important error boundaries.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Adding caching, indexes or replicas before locating the time spent or defining the symptom.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you check if the API is slow only during peak traffic?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q033"></a>

### S05-Q033 · Failure cases

<p>How would you distinguish and investigate memory growth and ThreadPool starvation in a production .NET service?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q033](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q033)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q033](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q033)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you diagnose memory growth or ThreadPool starvation in production?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Treat the two symptoms as potentially different mechanisms. ThreadPool starvation concerns work waiting for available worker capacity; establish observations before choosing a remedy.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Select diagnostic evidence that differentiates resource symptoms and validates a hypothesis.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Identify the .NET runtime, hosting limits and available diagnostic access; avoid assuming every memory increase is a leak. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Builds separate hypotheses for the two symptoms and selects discriminating observations.</li>
<li>Explains a low-risk capture or comparison that can confirm the suspected mechanism.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Recommending more memory or threads based only on one utilization graph.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would make you reject the hypothesis that increased memory usage is a managed-object leak?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S01-Q046"></a>

### S01-Q046 · Failure cases

<p>Under many concurrent requests, how would you identify the actual bottleneck in a .NET application? Explain the evidence that distinguishes your leading hypotheses.</p>

**Source:** [S01-Q046](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q046)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S01-Q046](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q046)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How would you identify a bottleneck under a large number of concurrent requests?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Start with the observed latency or throughput symptom and trace the request path. A bottleneck is a limiting resource or stage, not a component guessed from its name.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design an evidence-led performance investigation.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State the load pattern, comparable baseline and affected request class; observations and benchmark results must be real, not invented.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects request timing with resource, queue or dependency evidence.</li>
<li>Chooses a discriminating check and validates the repair under comparable load.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Recommending caching or more replicas before locating the limiting stage.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would make you rule out CPU saturation as the primary cause?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A hypothetical API’s p99 latency rises while its average changes little. Design the evidence to follow a request from frontend through gateway and service to database, including correlation and safe logs. Compare downstream delay, CPU, retained memory and worker pressure, then define a falsifying check and a comparable verification run.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Distinguishes telemetry types and locates relevant request and resource observations.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Uses correlated evidence and competing hypotheses, including tails and safe production collection.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>An average latency value or a trace screenshot alone does not establish causality or a verified repair.</p>
